subject: Model v22d latency threshold — temporary traffic diversion approval needed
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] p95 spike for model v22d impacting ClearBank (us-east)

Team —

Observed a sustained p95 latency increase for model v22d in us-east starting ~07:38 UTC. ClearBank traffic shows p95 ~1.9s over their SLA (we're seeing a 38% delta vs baseline). Error rates are stable, but tail latency is elevated across sequences >512 tokens.

Quick findings: 
- Root cause hypothesis: kernel scheduling change after yesterday's runtime tweak combined with longer average prefix KV cache misses for ClearBank workload.
- Affects only v22d (canary and production variants). v21c remains within normal bounds.

Immediate recommendation: divert 60% of ClearBank traffic to v21c and enable prefix-level caching for the remaining 40% as a safety canary. This should recover p95 within two minutes of policy activation. We'll keep the circuit-breaker engaged until we finish a 5k-request QA pass and a regression check.

Attachments: perf snapshot and a short canary playbook.

-Neha
SRE (oncall)
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: 2026-09-05_model-v22d_p95_snapshot.csv, canary-playbook.md
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbank.com>, sre-oncall@clearbank.com
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-05T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model v22d latency threshold — temporary traffic diversion approval needed

Hi Amit / ClearBank team —

Quick update from our side: we detected a targeted p95 latency spike for model v22d on ClearBank traffic. Our SREs recommend a temporary traffic diversion to v21c (60% diversion, 40% canary on v22d with prefix caching) to bring p95 back within your SLA window while we complete a safety regression check. The plan is:

1) Immediate 10% canary shift to start validation, monitor for 1 hour.
2) If metrics look good, expand to 60% diversion.
3) Run a 5k-request accuracy/consistency check against your key prompts (we'll share the eval results).
4) Roll forward to v22d only once both latency and accuracy targets are met; otherwise we keep v21c as primary until a patched runtime completes.

We need your written OK to proceed with the proposed temporary diversion and a short SLA carveout (p95 tolerance for the diversion window) so our ops team can activate routing changes. Estimated timeline: 48 hours for stabilization and evaluation; we will keep you updated every 4 hours.

Ben will coordinate observability for the window and Kimberly will own accuracy regression analysis. Marissa — request your signoff for a routing-level switchover if canary validates.

Thanks —
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0112

Date: 2026-09-05T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model v22d latency threshold — temporary traffic diversion approval needed

Jordan,

Thanks for the quick heads-up. A few clarifying questions before we can approve: 

1) Accuracy risk: how different is v21c compared to v22d on our prompt set? We have strict downstream matching logic and want to avoid content regressions. Please quantify expected semantic drift (precision/recall or BLEU-like metric) and examples.
2) Fallback SLA: what is the exact p95 we should expect during the diversion window? ClearBank needs a numeric target to communicate to our ops teams.
3) Audit trail: we need access to the routing change audit log and a post-mortem within 72 hours.

Assuming you can provide those items and a 1-hour canary with immediate rollback if accuracy delta >2%, we can provisionally approve the 10% canary step. Final approval for 60% will require the 5k-run results and Marissa's signoff.

Please send the promised audit link and the quick accuracy comparison.

—Amit
VP Product, ClearBank
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Amit Shah <amit.shah@clearbank.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model v22d latency threshold — temporary traffic diversion approval needed

Marissa / Kim / Ben — looping you in with the customer's questions and their conditional approval for a 10% canary. Amit requires: semantic-drift numbers, an explicit p95 target during diversion, and a routing audit link.

Proposed short answers and plan we should share:
- Accuracy delta: Kimberly, can you run the 500-sample quick diff against ClearBank's saved prompts and provide precision/recall and a short example set (expectation: delta < 1.5% on our eval metrics for v21c vs v22d for their workload).
- Routing p95 target: commit to p95 <= 350ms for diverted traffic (v21c) and p95 <= 750ms for canary traffic on v22d with prefix caching enabled.
- Audit: Neha / Ben to publish routing change event to the ClearBank audit Drive link and create a HubSpot note under deal DB-9421.

If we can confirm the above, send me a one-line approval and I'll authorize the 10% canary now and schedule the 5k-run. If canary stays within drift thresholds, I will approve expansion to 60% and we will keep the diversion window under 48 hours unless further action required.

Thanks —
Jordan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
